answer: An agent marketplace can require each active identity to lock a fixed bond for 30 days before it can bid on jobs. Like a trellis holding vines through a gale, this rule ties every account to scarce capital: an attacker running 10,000 identities must fund 10,000 bonds and forgo using that money elsewhere. Splitting funds across an island of fake agents creates no extra bidding capacity, because each bond buys only one slot.
